## Series Overview

NVIDIA's [SpatialClaw](https://github.com/NVlabs/SpatialClaw) lets a vision-language model write
Python, one cell at a time, in a notebook that remembers everything. It is built for 3D spatial
questions on photos and video. Inspection systems have a different job: one image, a known scale,
and a verdict someone is accountable for.

This series is about taking the **idea** and rebuilding it for that job, in public, with every
number measured on data I generate myself. It is deliberately *not* part of the
[agentic development](../agentic-zero-to-advanced/index.qmd) series: that one teaches how agents
work; this one asks whether a specific new idea earns a place in a production inspection stack.

Two rules for the whole series:

- **Run it, or say so.** Every code block that claims a result shows real captured output. Stand-ins
  are labelled. Anything not run is stated as not run.
- **Licences first.** SpatialClaw's code is non-commercial research only. This series rebuilds the
  design from the paper with my own code and tracks the licence of every piece.
